questions.q: Identify the sensory imagery in this line from the story: "इहरी धुंध में लिपटी ठंडी हवा के झोंके जब-तब खिड़कियों से टकराते हुए कमरे में घुस आते थे।" Name the specific sense(s) appealed to and quote the exact words.
questions.a: Correct answer: Tactile imagery (touch) — "ठंडी हवा के झोंके" (cold gusts of wind) and "कमरे में घुस आते थे" (entered the room) create a physical sensation of cold air hitting the skin. Visual imagery — "इहरी धुंध" (dense fog) and "खिड़कियों से टकराते हुए" (colliding with windows) create a mental picture. A wrong answer that only says "imagery of cold" without naming the specific sense (tactile/visual) or quoting exact words reveals the student cannot distinguish between sensory types or anchor analysis in textual evidence — a critical Board exam requirement.

questions.q: Explain in your own words the metaphor in this passage: "लाहको अंगीठी के सामने बैठा अपनी ठिठुरी हुई उँगलियों को ताप रहा था। अंगीठी की आग उसके भीतर की ठंड को भी पिघलाने की कोशिश कर रही थी।" Identify the tenor and vehicle, and state what quality is transferred.
questions.a: Correct answer: Tenor = लाहको की आंतरिक निराशा/रचनात्मक ठहराव (Lahko's inner despair/creative stagnation); Vehicle = "भीतर की ठंड" (inner cold) and "अंगीठी की आग" (fireplace fire). Quality transferred: Fire's ability to melt/transform is attributed to the writer's creative spark attempting to overcome emotional numbness. A wrong answer that identifies tenor as "Lahko's cold hands" misses the metaphorical layer — the text explicitly separates physical cold ("ठिठुरी हुई उँगलियों") from inner cold ("भीतर की ठंड"), so confusing literal and figurative levels shows inability to distinguish denotative vs. connotative meaning.

questions.q: Apply the concept: In the scene where Yashoda serves food to the child (pages 124-125), find ONE olfactory (smell) and ONE gustatory (taste) image. Quote the exact phrases and explain how they contrast with the earlier imagery of scarcity.
questions.a:
Correct answer steps: 
1. Locate the meal scene: "यशोदा ने थाली में दाल-चावल परोसे... घी की महक..." 
2. Olfactory: "घी की महक" (smell of ghee) — rich, warm, nourishing aroma.
3. Gustatory: "दाल-चावल" (lentils and rice) with "घी" implies taste of comfort food.
4. Contrast: Earlier imagery — "ब्रेड के टुकड़े" (bread pieces), "चाय" (tea), "खाली पेट" (empty stomach) — conveys scarcity, meagerness. The ghee/daal-chawal imagery signals temporary abundance, human care, dignity restored. A wrong answer quoting only "खाना" (food) without sensory-specific words shows inability to discriminate sensory modes — a common error where students lump all food references as "imagery" without analyzing the sensory shift that marks thematic turning points.

questions.q: Analyze the extended metaphor of "अंगीठी" (fireplace) across the story. Trace its appearances in at least three scenes and explain how its metaphorical meaning evolves from physical warmth to creative sustenance to human connection.
questions.a:
Correct answer: 
Scene 1 (p.118): "लाहको अंगीठी के सामने बैठा..." — literal physical warmth for frozen fingers; metaphor: survival of the body.
Scene 2 (p.120): "अंगीठी की आग उसके भीतर की ठंड को भी पिघलाने की कोशिश कर रही थी" — metaphor shifts to creative thawing; fire = writer's spark.
Scene 3 (p.124): "लाहको ने अंगीठी में लकड़ियाँ डालीं... यशोदा और बच्चे भी पास आ बैठे" — fire becomes communal hearth; metaphor: shared humanity, dignity in poverty.
Evolution: Body → Mind → Community. A wrong answer listing scenes without explaining the *semantic shift* (literal → psychological → social) treats metaphor as static decoration rather than a dynamic thematic engine — exactly what Board examiners penalize in "analyze" level questions.

questions.q: Evaluate this student interpretation: "The metaphor 'जिंदगी एक अंगीठी है' (Life is a fireplace) is the central metaphor of the story because the fireplace appears in every major scene." Defend or refute using textual evidence.
questions.a: Correct answer: Refute. The story never explicitly states "जिंदगी एक अंगीठी है" — this is a student-invented generalization, not a textual metaphor. The fireplace functions as a *recurring image* that *acquires* metaphorical resonance through context (as shown in Q4), but it is not a declared metaphor with tenor "life." Central metaphors in the story are implicit: "भीतर की ठंड" (inner cold = creative death), "राख" (ash = spent creativity), "चिंगारी" (spark = hope). A wrong answer that accepts the invented metaphor reveals inability to distinguish between *author's crafted metaphors* and *reader's thematic summaries* — a fatal error in competitive exams where precise textual grounding is mandatory.

questions.q: Create a new metaphor for Lahko's writing process using imagery from the story (cold, fire, ash, paper, night). Write it as a single sentence and explain the tenor, vehicle, and transferred quality.
questions.a:
Expected answer criteria: 
- Original metaphor sentence, e.g., "उसकी कलम अंगीठी की वह आखिरी चिंगारी थी जो राख में भी साँस लेती रही।" (His pen was that last spark in the fireplace that kept breathing even in ash.)
- Tenor: Lahko's writing process / creative persistence
- Vehicle: "आखिरी चिंगारी" (last spark) in "राख" (ash)
- Transferred quality: Capacity to survive/ignite in seemingly dead conditions
- Must use story-specific imagery (not generic "light in darkness")
Poor answer: "Writing is like fire" (simile, not metaphor; generic; no story-specific imagery). This reveals confusion between simile/metaphor, inability to extract story-specific image clusters, and failure to articulate tenor-vehicle mechanics.
